problems.statement: The 98.1% on-time figure is largely an artifact of the KPI definition, which lets dispatchers overwrite the promised date and measures against the revised date, combined with a bonus that rewards the number; it is not a reliable measure of delivery performance.

Real service has not improved and has probably worsened: Brightwell's receiving logs show 81% on time against the original date (down from 87%), lateness complaints rose 35% against a 4% rise in volume, and the customer is moving 30% of its lanes to tender.
Revisions are mostly legitimate customer requests or weather, as the Northgate manager claims.
The complaint rise is only a portal reporting effect and does not indicate worse service.

A driver shortage on mountain lanes is a real operational problem. It drives some genuine lateness and some Operational-Capacity revisions, but it does not explain the network-wide step change in revisions.

Organizational problem: the incentive was tied to a metric that the same people can edit, with no controls, audit, or customer-notification requirement. Supervisors reinforce protecting the number, and few dispatchers raise concerns.
The proposed campaign and raised 99% bonus tier would amplify the problem, creating false-advertising and reputational risk and stronger incentives to revise dates.

causalClaims.from: Dispatcher bonus plan tied to on-time % (effective Mar 2026, Jul at Pell Junction) with no change to revision controls
causalClaims.to: Surge in promised-date revisions (about 5x), shifted to Operational-Capacity and late-entered
Reported on-time rise from about 91% to about 98%

causalClaims.from: Revision surge and low customer notification
causalClaims.to: Customer-experienced lateness and complaints, and Brightwell's tender threat

actions.action: Postpone the 12 January '98 out of 100, on time' campaign and do not publish the claim until it is re-measured against original promised dates.
actions.rationale: The claim is not supported by customer-side data and risks false advertising and reputational damage, while a postponement costs little and can be reversed.

actions.action: Do not raise the top bonus tier to $1,500 at 99%; freeze or suspend the on-time bonus as currently defined.
actions.rationale: It would intensify the incentive to edit dates on a gameable metric.

actions.action: Report on-time against the original promised date (and the customer-requested date) alongside the revised-date figure. Restate the 2025 baseline on the same basis.
actions.rationale: The original dates are retained in the revision log, so a corrected KPI can be produced quickly and cheaply.

actions.action: Add revision controls: require Notify Customer, require approval for revisions made late or tagged Operational-Capacity, audit samples, and track revision rate as a guardrail metric.
actions.rationale: This targets the mechanism that produces the inflated figure.

actions.action: Redesign the dispatcher bonus around original-date on-time and customer-confirmed outcomes, with a protected channel for raising concerns.
actions.rationale: It removes the incentive to game the number but needs the re-based data first.

actions.action: Contact Brightwell and the other large accounts proactively with accurate data and a recovery plan before the Q1 review.
actions.rationale: It addresses the actual revenue risk, which is 30% of the largest customer's lanes.

actions.action: Address driver shortages on the mountain lanes (hiring and retention) after quantifying their share of genuine lateness.
actions.rationale: The shortage is a real but unquantified contributor and is separate from the metric problem.

actions.action: Attribute the improvement to RouteWise or treat the complaint increase as a portal artifact, and dismiss the concerns.
actions.rationale: The evidence counts against both explanations, and acting on them would entrench the problem.

actions.action: Discipline individual dispatchers for revising dates.
actions.rationale: The behavior follows from the incentive design and the supervisors' instruction, and discipline would drive concerns further underground.

nextEvidence: On-time % against the original promised date, by dispatch center and month, for Jan 2025 to Oct 2026, from the revision log, with a breakdown of revisions made after the original date had passed or made without customer notification
An audit of a sample of Operational-Capacity revisions against actual delivery dates and customer appointment records, plus equivalent receiving data from other large accounts
Complaint data split by channel and by lateness, with a portal-adjusted baseline, and an analysis of driver vacancy against late deliveries controlling for lane length
output.summary: The 98.1% figure is mainly produced by how it is measured. The bonus (from March 2026, July at Pell Junction) rewards on-time % against a date dispatchers can overwrite, with no new controls. Revisions rose about 5x and shifted to Operational-Capacity and late entry, and few customers were notified. The timing matches the bonus rollout at each center and not RouteWise, which went live at Northgate only in October. Brightwell's logs show 81% on time against the original date, down from 87%, and it is putting 30% of its lanes to tender. Lateness complaints rose 35% against 4% more volume. Pause the campaign and the higher bonus tier, re-baseline on original dates, add revision controls, and engage the large accounts.
